rv.q: In cullud wattah, Erika Dickerson-Despenza compellingly weaves the personal and political.

The noteworthy, unmistakable brilliance of cullud wattah is that the writer, director, and actors are like silhouettes in this production, choosing to have the audience focus more on the meaning than their contribution and performers, which can be seen during the impacting ending!
In this writer's view, Victory Gardens Theater, playwright Erika Dickerson-Despenza, Director Lili-Anne Brown and this super talented cast show the world what this really means.
Dickerson-Despenza has written an instant classic.

Her powerful story of three generations of Black women, now receiving a fiercely emotional regional premiere at Victory Gardens Theater, is a model for how to fully humanize a social and political crisis.

cn.t: Critics praise "cullud wattah" as a powerful, moving drama about the Flint water crisis, with strong performances and Erika Dickerson-Despenza's compelling script earning acclaim for its emotional resonance and urgent storytelling.
